claims.statement: JUCE 8.0.15 (commit 91ad83ae34a81e0833b1a2b0866f54846370ae53) is the final release of the 8.x line and the correct pin for v1; the 9.x line (newest 9.0.4) restructures the VST3 client extension API with 35+ breaking changes and is forbidden for v1. An 8.0.16-security patch tag exists and is evaluated at S-001. (Amended 2026-10-27 from the original '8.0.12 is current', which a live tag listing and knowledge item K-20261004T151500Z showed to be stale.)
Ableton Live 12 hosts 64-bit VST3 plugins on Windows and macOS (VST3 support since Live 10.1); AU is macOS-only; AAX is unsupported.
pluginval 2.0.0 validates VST3/AU plugins via CLI at configurable strictness levels and integrates the Steinberg VST3 validator and auval; it provides GitHub Actions composite actions for CI.
JUCE's AudioProcessorValueTreeState exposes parameters to hosts for automation and provides state save/restore via copyState/replaceState; smoothed gain changes via ramps avoid clicks.
JUCE builds VST3, AU, and Standalone targets from one CMake project definition.

Staged waveshaping with pre/de-emphasis filtering under oversampling, plus IR-based cabinet convolution, is a standard, proven architecture for non-neural guitar amp simulation spanning clean to high-gain tones.

Full circuit (WDF) modeling of 7 topologies or a neural-capture (NAM/LSTM) pipeline exceeds a solo developer's v1 budget; a parametric engine can ship first with a neural stage added later behind the same interface.
sources: planner domain assessment; S-8 for neural precedent

claims.statement: In JUCE VST3 plugins, loading presets via per-parameter setValueNotifyingHost/performEdit can cause hosts (Ableton Live among them) to record spurious automation; preset loads should use replaceState, and GUI edits should use begin/endChangeGesture.

JUCE 8 is dual-licensed under the JUCE licence and AGPLv3; free tiers: Starter (closed-source allowed, $20k revenue limit, no splash) and AGPL-3.0 for open source. Added 2026-10-27 by the Phase 4.7 audit (corrects the A-009 premise).

Mull 0.34.0 (May 2026) provides LLVM-IR mutation testing for C/C++ via version-matched mull-NN/clang-NN packages and a -fpass-plugin instrumented -O0 build; tests and third-party code must be excluded from mutation scope.
